title: Does the market get sharper toward the close?
headline_insight: For the WNBA, the devigged market's Brier score improves as the game nears -- from 0.245445 six hours out (T-6h) to 0.228045 at the close, across 30 games.
what_it_means: A sharper (lower) Brier at the close means the market is a better-calibrated forecaster the closer you get to tip -- consistent with fresh information arriving late. For international soccer the same test does not sharpen, but that read is underpowered (13 games) and provisional.
how_to_read: Each horizon bucket (T-24h, T-6h, T-1h, close) reports the Brier of the consensus devigged home-win probability scored against the settled result; lower is better and a downward step toward the close is the sharpening.
why_it_matters: It tells you how much the closing number is worth over an earlier snapshot -- the yardstick a forecaster has to match, and the window where late information is priced.
caveat: Single capture window -- provisional, not durable; soccer_intl is flagged underpowered; NBA, MLB, tennis and club soccer are not_joinable here (line_history ids do not key to an on-disk outcome table). edge_claimed false.
